subject.title: [Bug] v2026.6.11 published dist missing reentrancy guard - reply session initialization conflicted

question: Should maintainers publish a corrected stable package for the v2026.6.11 reply-session artifact failure, or hold this until the next stable release train?
rationale: The source fixes are present on current main, but users on npm `latest` still receive v2026.6.11; only maintainers can choose the stable release vehicle, versioning, and any affected-release notice.

options.title: Publish corrected stable
options.body: Cut a stable hotfix or next stable package and verify the packed artifact contains the reentrant writer plus reply-session identity-guard fixes.

options.title: Wait for next stable train
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical package-parity tracker until the next normal stable release ships and is verified.

options.title: Document affected release only
options.body: Leave v2026.6.11 as latest for now but clearly mark it affected and point users to a safe workaround or beta.

recommendation.title: Publish corrected stable
recommendation.body: Cut a stable hotfix or next stable package and verify the packed artifact contains the reentrant writer plus reply-session identity-guard fixes.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is release/package handling, and this person is tied to the latest stable release commit in local history.
